scope: Independent local source review only; no GPU execution or performance claim
manual_checks: A2A atomically compacted receive rows are mapped using exact BF16 hidden-state bytes, full original K8 IDs and FP32 score bytes. Valid receive rows preserve non-owner IDs; only unreceived padding rows have all IDs=E.

Mapping checks source-rank block, requires at least one owned route, rejects missing/duplicate/ambiguous/unmatched payloads and constructs independent expected partials in native receive order. It does not add timed payload or read production tracking metadata.

A2A reference places each independent BF16 owner partial at the first original top-k slot for that owner; duplicate slots are zero. It then applies the native K8 pairwise FP32 tree and one BF16 cast; no rank-order or NCCL reduction is substituted.
Split owner-local reference uses ascending original route slots with FP32 FMA and one BF16 cast. Gather variants use trusted actual NCCL BF16 SUM with the original padded collective shape.

Mega reference uses BF16 expert terms, initial FP32 multiplication then ordered FP32 FMAs and final BF16 cast. Independent expert math decodes canonical NVFP4 weights and uses cuBLASLt FP32-output GEMMs plus source-matched SwiGLU.
Input and route identity is exact and cannot be waived by output tolerances. Padding and zero-token source ranks remain valid, with all-rank error reduction.

Original cross-pair CSV PASS/FAIL remains visible; default cross-pair policy still raises on FAIL. Per-path policy is explicit, preserves atol=rtol=.01, and requires independent per-variant checks before latency acceptance.

Reference outputs retained for the oracle are CPU tensors; temporary GPU work is outside unchanged timed callables. Additional setup changes allocator/cache history and is part of the new r4 methodology, not identical r3 execution state.
